issues.legal_issue: An agreement is unenforceable for stifling a criminal prosecution only when discontinuance of the prosecution is the consideration, or part of the consideration, for the other party’s promise.
material_facts: The dispute concerned documents executed in favour of a bank after it had lodged a criminal complaint and while the police were investigating.
The complaint was dropped after the bank reported that its claim had been settled.
issues.conclusion: An agreement supported by a promise to discontinue criminal proceedings is opposed to public policy and unenforceable, but the party challenging it must prove that the promise to discontinue was the consideration for the agreement. The doctrine does not apply to compoundable offences, or to offences compounded with the court’s leave.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, agreements whose consideration or object is opposed to public policy are unenforceable. Agreements made with the consideration that a complainant will discontinue criminal proceedings are opposed to public policy, subject to the exception for compoundable offences and offences compounded with the court’s leave. The court must distinguish the parties’ motive from the agreement’s consideration; sequence of events alone does not establish the prohibited consideration. The court relied on V. Narasimha Raju v. V. Gurumurthy Raju, [1963] 3 S.C.R. 687; Maharaja Srish Chandra Nandy v. Supravat Chandra, A.I.R. 1940 Cal. 337; Sudhindra Kumar Ray Chaudhuri v. Ganesh Chandra Ganguli, 1939 I.L.R. I Cal. 241; Kamini Kumar Basu v. Birendra Nath Basu, A.I.R. 1930 P.C. 100; and considered Bhowanipur Banking Corporation Ltd. v. Durgesh Nandini Dasi, (1942) I.L.R. 1 Cal. 1.

predicates.agreement_challenged_as_stifling_prosecu: A party to an agreement challenges its enforceability on the ground that it was made to stop a criminal prosecution.
predicates.noncompoundable_offence: The criminal proceeding concerned an offence that could not be compounded.
predicates.compounding_without_required_court_leave: The parties sought to compound an offence requiring court leave without obtaining that leave.
predicates.promise_exchanged_for_discontinuance: One party promised consideration in exchange for the complainant’s promise to discontinue the criminal proceeding.

issues.definition: When an agreement challenged as stopping a prosecution concerns a non-compoundable offence or an unapproved compounding, and discontinuance was exchanged for a promise, the agreement is unenforceable as opposed to public policy.

issues.legal_issue: Security documents executed after a criminal complaint are not unenforceable for stifling prosecution unless the challengers prove that the security was given in exchange for discontinuance of the criminal proceeding.
material_facts: Borrowers owed the bank money secured by pledged goods, and an inspection revealed that the goods in the godown were insufficient to cover the debt.
The bank complained to the police, alleging that goods had been removed or that the pledged security had been inadequate.
Before the complaint was filed, the borrowers had offered to provide additional security and delivered some title documents to the bank.

After the complaint was filed, family members executed a hypothecation bond and a further agreement in favour of the bank; the bank then reported settlement of its claim, and the criminal proceeding was dropped.
The borrowers did not testify, and the court found the evidence offered to prove an agreement to withdraw the complaint in exchange for the documents unsatisfactory.
The borrowers later sought further credit from the bank; they also did not challenge the validity of a related hire-purchase agreement in the bank’s suit concerning it.
issues.conclusion: The challengers failed to prove that the documents were executed in exchange for discontinuance of the criminal proceeding. The documents were therefore not unenforceable on that ground, and the High Court’s dismissal of the cancellation suit and decree in the bank’s recovery suit were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The party impugning a transaction under section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 bears the strict burden of proving that it was based on an agreement to stifle prosecution. The court must determine whether discontinuance was the consideration for the promise, not merely a motive or an event that followed the transaction. A prior agreement to furnish additional security, inadequate pledged goods, the challengers’ failure to testify, and the unsatisfactory quality of their evidence were relevant to whether that burden was met. The governing authorities include V. Narasimha Raju v. V. Gurumurthy Raju, [1963] 3 S.C.R. 687; Maharaja Srish Chandra Nandy v. Supravat Chandra, A.I.R. 1940 Cal. 337; Sudhindra Kumar Ray Chaudhuri v. Ganesh Chandra Ganguli, 1939 I.L.R. I Cal. 241; Kamini Kumar Basu v. Birendra Nath Basu, A.I.R. 1930 P.C. 100; and Bhowanipur Banking Corporation Ltd. v. Durgesh Nandini Dasi, (1942) I.L.R. 1 Cal. 1.

rule.if: civil_proceeding_challenges_security_documents_as_stifling_prosecution and additional_security_offered_before_complaint and pledged_goods_inadequate and challengers_failed_to_testify and evidence_of_exchange_unsatisfactory

predicates.civil_proceeding_challenges_security_doc: A civil proceeding seeks to cancel or resist enforcement of security documents on the ground that they were executed to stop a criminal prosecution.
predicates.additional_security_offered_before_compl: The debtors offered to provide additional security before the criminal complaint was filed.
predicates.pledged_goods_inadequate: The goods held as security were insufficient to cover the debt.
predicates.challengers_failed_to_testify: The parties challenging the documents did not give evidence themselves on the alleged agreement.
predicates.evidence_of_exchange_unsatisfactory: The evidence presented by the challengers did not satisfactorily show that the documents were exchanged for discontinuance of the criminal proceeding.

issues.definition: In a civil challenge to security documents, where additional security was offered before the complaint, the pledged goods were inadequate, the challengers did not testify, and evidence of an exchange was unsatisfactory, the documents are not proven unenforceable for stifling prosecution.
